outside.waitsOn: ARCH: the facility list
tests: R1: discoverMembers lists every member of a repository, each with its directory and entry point, in a stable order
R1: a marker that cannot be read as JSON is an error naming it, never a member silently dropped
R1: the repository's own fleet is discovered with each member's directory and entry point
R2: one recipe: ES module output, platform-neutral, the declared externals, cwd pinned, symlinks preserved
R2: the built bytes are an ES module that bundles first-party and vendored code and keeps only the declared externals
R2: the same source gives the same bytes from any working directory and any checkout layout
R3: buildMember writes the artifact only when write is true
R4: the manifest records the artifact's SHA-256, every first-party input's, the lockfile's, and the pinned working directory
R5: writeMember builds with writing on and writes the artifact and its manifest
R6: with no dependencies installed, a changed input or lockfile is reported stale, naming the input
R6: a vendored input that is present and changed, a moved artifact, or a changed recipe is stale too
R7: with dependencies installed, a fresh build must equal the committed bytes exactly
R7: where the dependencies are not installed it says it could not check, never that the artifact is fresh
R8: every import specifier that is neither bundled nor an allowed external is listed, once, sorted
R8: a fully bundled artifact lists nothing, and one with an undeclared external lists it
R9: each file is stated committed and unchanged, changed, staged, or untracked, and reported
R9: where git cannot answer, every file is UNVERIFIED and the report says so, never clean
R10: no verifying call creates or changes a file, fresh or stale, installed or not
R10: verifying the repository's own fleet writes nothing
R24: a marker with kind container and an image block is a container member, listed with its kind and its image; every other member is listed as a worker

R24: verifyStatic and verifyFresh never report a container member with no Worker bundle stale, unguarded or missing an artifact, and say it is not guarded; one that states no image is still named unguarded
R24: a container member that declares a Worker bundle is guarded like any member: built, verified, and named stale when its source moves
R24: the repository's own fleet lists agent-runner as a container member with its image, and only a container member goes unguarded
R25: containerDescriptor writes the part from the marker — class_name, image as <repository>@sha256:<64 hex>, scheduling_policy default, max_instances, bind — and names every field it lacks
R25: imageReference names the image only by digest, in agent-runner R7's form, or names the field that does not say it
R24: a container member stating its classes as a `containers` list, each with its own image, is a container member, listed with each class's name and image

R25: a member with more than one class gets one Container part per class, container/<class>.json, each its own class_name and image, max_instances and bind from the class else the member; one class is container.json as before
R25: a class lacking a field is refused naming the class and every field; a duplicated class, both forms at once, or no bundle are refused too

R27: a class naming a package statement reads its packages from it, sorted, under the ecosystem it names, only when its base digest is the marker's; otherwise unread naming the file, the package or the digest

R25: workerPart writes {r2_buckets, crons} from a member's config, each bucket by its role and the crons as stated; none for a member with neither; every binding with no role, and every list that is not one, named
R25: the repository's own members with buckets or crons carry a Worker part, every bucket with a role; file-scanner's names CAPTURES and its daily schedule

R25 (K4094): workerPart states a member's own Durable Objects and migrations in order, each migration as {tag, classes}; another script's object (script_name) is not the member's and is left out; a part the Durable Objects alone need is written, and a member owning none is not

R25 (K4094): over the repository's own fleet, each member's Worker part states the Durable Objects its configuration owns: agent-worker its two, agent-runner its one binding and every migration it declares, file-scanner its two

R35: the real fleet's three container images (agent-runner's, file-scanner's two classes) are named docker.io/civicsmith/<repository>@sha256:<64 hex> by their markers, and the part R25 writes carries that address

R35: R24's and R25's fixtures name docker.io/<org>/…@sha256 markers and are listed and written as stated; control: a marker naming another registry is written as stated by R25, and the real-fleet test fails on it

R37: a class whose image files match what its recorded digest was built from is current; a changed byte in a copied file, an added file in a copied directory, a changed Dockerfile, or a file removed from a copied directory is stale, naming the class; a file the Dockerfile does not copy, and a COPY --from, change nothing

R37: a marker that records nothing its digest was built from, or a source that is not a 64-hex digest, is unrecorded; a Dockerfile naming no file, copying a wildcard or an address, or a marker naming no Dockerfile, is unread

R36: recording the digest a build produced writes it, and the files it was built from, into the marker's image block and the digest into the image the wrangler.jsonc container block names, both agreeing, keeping the wrangler comments and repository; the class is current afterwards
R36: a member with two classes records the digest of the class named and leaves the other's digest, source and image as they were

R36: a digest that is not sha256:<64 hex> (CONTAINER_DIGEST_INVALID), a class the member does not state, a member that is not a container member, a wrangler.jsonc naming no digest image for the class, and a Dockerfile that cannot be hashed are each refused, with neither file written
R36 (T51-144): over the real fleet, each container class's fleet-member.json image.digest is the digest its wrangler.jsonc containers[] entry names, so a cut cannot leave one stale
R36 (T51-144): control: a fixture whose two digests differ fails the agreement test naming the member and the class; the same fixture with them equal passes
R38: a member's bundle carries exactly the rows its inputs name at word, localize and hasWord calls, in the table's order, and its manifest records their count and digest
R38: control: a key built from a literal prefix ('refusal.' + code, or a template) keeps every row under that prefix
R38: control: a key read from a bare variable keeps the whole table for that member, names every such site by file and line in its manifest (words: all), and the build does not fail

R38: control: a read that is not a call (word used as a value, the whole table imported, a dynamic import) keeps the whole table naming the site; a word, localize or hasWord the file declares itself is not the call

R38: the plane's bundle is unchanged: the plane carries the whole table, records no word rows, and is built by the plain recipe; a member whose inputs do not reach the table builds as before and records none
R38: verifyFresh covers the rows kept: a manifest that records other rows than a fresh build keeps is stale, and one that records them is fresh

R38: over the real fleet, each member that builds carries only the rows its inputs name (each member's row count stated); the bundles' keys are all named by literal at a call or under a literal prefix of its inputs
R38: over the real fleet, a member whose inputs hold a word read with a variable key keeps the whole table and its manifest names the sites by file and line (agent-worker today; K3958)

R39: every kind of binding is held to what the release exports: a service names the plane or a member; a Durable Object with a script_name names a member whose bundle exports the class, one without names its own bundle's; a container class and each class a migration creates, renames to or transfers are exported by the member's own bundle
R39: bundleExports reads the names the built bundle exports from the build, not from the source

R39: over the real fleet as it stands, every service and Durable Object binding the plane's and each member's configuration declares names a class or service the release exports (red by name until agent-runner exports RemoteSession, K4176)

tests: R1: discoverMembers lists every member of a repository, each with its directory and entry point, in a stable order
R1: a marker that cannot be read as JSON is an error naming it, never a member silently dropped
R1: the repository's own fleet is discovered with each member's directory and entry point
R2: one recipe: ES module output, platform-neutral, the declared externals, cwd pinned, symlinks preserved
R2: the built bytes are an ES module that bundles first-party and vendored code and keeps only the declared externals
R2: the same source gives the same bytes from any working directory and any checkout layout
R3: buildMember writes the artifact only when write is true
R4: the manifest records the artifact's SHA-256, every first-party input's, the lockfile's, and the pinned working directory
R5: writeMember builds with writing on and writes the artifact and its manifest
R6: with no dependencies installed, a changed input or lockfile is reported stale, naming the input
R6: a vendored input that is present and changed, a moved artifact, or a changed recipe is stale too
R7: with dependencies installed, a fresh build must equal the committed bytes exactly
R7: where the dependencies are not installed it says it could not check, never that the artifact is fresh
R8: every import specifier that is neither bundled nor an allowed external is listed, once, sorted
R8: a fully bundled artifact lists nothing, and one with an undeclared external lists it
R9: each file is stated committed and unchanged, changed, staged, or untracked, and reported
R9: where git cannot answer, every file is UNVERIFIED and the report says so, never clean
R10: no verifying call creates or changes a file, fresh or stale, installed or not
R10: verifying the repository's own fleet writes nothing
R24: a marker with kind container and an image block is a container member, listed with its kind and its image; every other member is listed as a worker

R24: verifyStatic and verifyFresh never report a container member with no Worker bundle stale, unguarded or missing an artifact, and say it is not guarded; one that states no image is still named unguarded
R24: a container member that declares a Worker bundle is guarded like any member: built, verified, and named stale when its source moves
R24: the repository's own fleet lists agent-runner as a container member with its image, and only a container member goes unguarded
R25: containerDescriptor writes the part from the marker — class_name, image as <repository>@sha256:<64 hex>, scheduling_policy default, max_instances, bind — and names every field it lacks
R25: imageReference names the image only by digest, in agent-runner R7's form, or names the field that does not say it
R24: a container member stating its classes as a `containers` list, each with its own image, is a container member, listed with each class's name and image

R25: a member with more than one class gets one Container part per class, container/<class>.json, each its own class_name and image, max_instances and bind from the class else the member; one class is container.json as before
R25: a class lacking a field is refused naming the class and every field; a duplicated class, both forms at once, or no bundle are refused too

R18: the upload's metadata carries observability {enabled: true} derived from wrangler.jsonc, and success is stated only after the script's settings read back as enabled, before the schedules are set

R18: a read-back whose settings report Workers Logs off, absent, different or unreadable refuses success [OBSERVABILITY_MISMATCH | OBSERVABILITY_UNREADABLE], exit 1, with no schedules set and no rollout wait

R18: a wrangler.jsonc that does not turn Workers Logs on, or carries a key the derivation does not, is refused before any request, as one without a subrequest ceiling is; --dry-run refuses the same way
R34: identical bytes serving the version with matching limits, bindings and schedules are still a metadata deploy while the script's Workers Logs are not on; with them on it uploads nothing
R40: --dry-run prints the observability the upload would send and what the script reports now, and sends nothing but reads
R41: runtime-limits' STORE_HINTS exists to validate against (red by name until that provider has merged)
R41: deriveStorePlace emits each flag as a plain_text binding, refuses a bad hint or generation by name, and sends nothing for an absent flag; generation 1 sends none and removes the held one
R41: --store-location and --store-generation are sent as plain_text bindings, each the value given; neither flag's value is read as a positional argument
R41: every hint of runtime-limits' list is accepted, and a value not on it is refused [BAD_STORE_LOCATION] before any request
R41: a generation that is not /^[1-9][0-9]*$/ is refused [BAD_STORE_GENERATION] before any request; controls: 2 and 10 are sent
R41: with no flag no store binding is sent, and a held STORE_LOCATION and STORE_GENERATION are kept unchanged (R34's rule)
R41: --store-generation 1 sends no STORE_GENERATION and removes a held one (the rollback), keeping a held STORE_LOCATION; a flag differing from the held value is a metadata deploy
R42: after the upload's answer the deploy prints `test deploy: startup <ms> ms` with the documented field result.startup_time_ms, after the upload and not before it
R42: an answer without the field, or with one that is not a number, prints `test deploy: startup unreported` and the deploy still succeeds

R18: the upload's metadata carries observability {enabled: true} derived from wrangler.jsonc, and success is stated only after the script's settings read back as enabled, before the schedules are set

R18: a read-back whose settings report Workers Logs off, absent, different or unreadable refuses success [OBSERVABILITY_MISMATCH | OBSERVABILITY_UNREADABLE], exit 1, with no schedules set and no rollout wait

R18: a wrangler.jsonc that does not turn Workers Logs on, or carries a key the derivation does not, is refused before any request, as one without a subrequest ceiling is; --dry-run refuses the same way
R34: identical bytes serving the version with matching limits, bindings and schedules are still a metadata deploy while the script's Workers Logs are not on; with them on it uploads nothing
R40: --dry-run prints the observability the upload would send and what the script reports now, and sends nothing but reads
R41: runtime-limits' STORE_HINTS exists to validate against (red by name until that provider has merged)
R41: deriveStorePlace emits each flag as a plain_text binding, refuses a bad hint or generation by name, and sends nothing for an absent flag; generation 1 sends none and removes the held one
R41: --store-location and --store-generation are sent as plain_text bindings, each the value given; neither flag's value is read as a positional argument
R41: every hint of runtime-limits' list is accepted, and a value not on it is refused [BAD_STORE_LOCATION] before any request
R41: a generation that is not /^[1-9][0-9]*$/ is refused [BAD_STORE_GENERATION] before any request; controls: 2 and 10 are sent
R41: with no flag no store binding is sent, and a held STORE_LOCATION and STORE_GENERATION are kept unchanged (R34's rule)
R41: --store-generation 1 sends no STORE_GENERATION and removes a held one (the rollback), keeping a held STORE_LOCATION; a flag differing from the held value is a metadata deploy
R42: after the upload's answer the deploy prints `test deploy: startup <ms> ms` with the documented field result.startup_time_ms, after the upload and not before it
R42: an answer without the field, or with one that is not a number, prints `test deploy: startup unreported` and the deploy still succeeds
